thread_title: S. x moorei 'Red Throat' Southern Baldwin Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. x moorei 'Red Throat' Southern Baldwin Co, AL

posts.body_html:
The red throat is a DEAD GIVEAWAY that this isn't a pure leucophylla. This particular clone of S. x moorei is pretty darn amazing in the sense that to an untrained eye (ie. anyone who doesn't regularly post or lurk on this forum), it looks like a pure S. leucophylla, but we all know because of that red throat and the slight difference in pitcher shape that it's a leuco x flava rugelii cross.

Photos taken 9/25/15. From this first shot, even a trained eye can mistake this for a pure S. leucophylla:


But as soon as you see this, you know there's flava rugelii up in the mix:


Can't wait for this thing to get bigger! The summer traps were still juvenile-ish in size so there wasn't anything to photograph until now. It'll be interesting to see if this clone can produce some stunning summer traps next year:


To be continued....

posts.body_html:
Very cool meizzwang! Ran across a few plants like this out in the bawgs this summer. With all the back-crossing out there they are bound to pop up! 
This one is from Santa Rosa Co FL. Shows some definite flava shape influence but one still might be tempted to call it a "leuco" without the throat patch:

Different clone, same site. This particular bog is quite extensive and is home to a massive moorei hybrid swarm. Interestingly, S. x Adrian Slack was collected in a now-destroyed portion of this large savanna. 

Same clone:

This plant is from Okaloosa Co and dang there is NO WAY you would suspect it has flava in it if it didn't have the remnant blotch. Tricky tricky!
